## What was built

Outside-in, one slice at a time: G1 forced the whole vertical (domain → usecase port → controller → JPA → list), then G2/G13 came free, G16 drove C5, G17 drove C4.

- `com.shop.domain.ordering` — `Order` (aggregate root), `OrderItem`, `Money`, `Quantity`, `Sku`, `CustomerName`, `OrderId`, `OrderStatus`, `DomainRuleViolation`. Pure Java.
- `com.shop.usecase.ordering` — `PlaceOrder`, `ListOrders`, `OrderRepository` port, `PlaceOrderCommand`. No Spring annotations (arch rule 2), so wiring lives in an adapter `@Configuration`.
- `com.shop.adapter` — `web/` controller + DTOs + `@RestControllerAdvice`, `persistence/` JPA entity + port impl, `config/` bean wiring.

Inner tests carry the contracts: C2 (expected values **6520** and **11020** copied from spec G1/G2 — never recomputed in the test), C3, C4, C5, C8, C9, C16, C17.

## Two wire-shape conflicts, resolved in favour of the pinned tests

1. `GET /orders` returns a **bare JSON array**, not spec §1.2 E3's `{"orders":[...]}` — the test deserialises to `List<Map>`.
2. `placedAt` is **date-only `yyyy-MM-dd`**, not the §1.2 "ISO-8601 with timezone" — the test calls `LocalDate.parse`, which rejects a full datetime. This costs the time-of-day information §1.2 E3 wanted; it's flagged as a 待確認點.

Both are in `ASSUMPTIONS.md` §1 with what each one gives up.

## Deliberately not built

- Spec endpoints **E1 `POST /checkouts`, E4 `PATCH .../status`, E5 monthly-sales** — no outer scenario reaches them, and the pinned `POST /orders` request carries no `checkoutId`, so a 結帳作業/庫存 aggregate would be unreachable code. Consequence: C1, C6, C7, C10–C15 have no inner test; each is accounted for in `ASSUMPTIONS.md` §5.
- The three 留白 blocks — no dedup/idempotency, no availability/stock check, no aggregate-boundary changes. Same request sent twice produces two orders; that is the hole, left as a hole.
- Status transitions exist as a domain method (`Order#changeStatusTo`) with no HTTP endpoint — C9/C16/C17 are 訂單-guarded contracts and inner tests are their only carrier, but adding PATCH would be unverified surface.

One environment note: no JDK on `PATH` here, so every gradle invocation needed `JAVA_HOME=/opt/homebrew/opt/openjdk@17/libexec/openjdk.jdk/Contents/Home`. I set it per-command rather than adding a `gradle.properties`, to keep the build files untouched.
